'''Ōmizu Shrine''' (大水神社) is an auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. This article also covers the subordinate shrines '''Kawaai Shrine''' (川相神社) and '''Kumabuchi Shrine''' (熊淵神社), which are co-located with Ōmizu Shrine.

All three shrines are said to have been established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}. Ōmizu Shrine enshrines a {{ill|Yama-no-Kami|ja|山の神|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mountain God|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q839254}}, while Kawaai Shrine and Kumabuchi Shrine enshrine {{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god}}.<ref>Gakken Publishing (2013): pp. 54–55</ref>

== Overview ==
These three shrines are located at Uji Imazai-kechō, Hayasakiguchi 163-1, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, about 200 meters from the {{ill|Uji Bridge (Ise City)|lt=Uji Bridge (Ise City)|lt=Uji Bridge (Ise)|ja|宇治橋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uji Bridge (Ise)|qq=}} at the entrance to the Inner Shrine's sacred precinct.<ref name="ic1">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 111</ref> About 50 meters ahead is {{ill|Aedo Hashihime Shrine|ja|饗土橋姫神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aedo Hashihime Shrine|qq=}}, and 70 meters ahead are the auxiliary shrines {{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunaga Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Nīkawa Shrine|ja|新川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkawa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11502105}}, and {{ill|Ishii Shrine|ja|石井神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishii Shrine|qq=}}, making a cluster of seven shrines.<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): pp. 111, 116</ref> The former {{ill|Jingū Library|ja|林崎文庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayasakibunko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮文庫|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11589490}}, predecessor of the {{ill|Jingū Library|ja|神宮文庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Library|qq=}}, is also located here.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 117</ref>

After ascending 12 stone steps, there is a {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shinmei torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}} and a single shrine building where all three shrines are co-located. An ancient camphor tree with a trunk diameter over 2 meters covers the shrine.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): pp. 54–55</ref> The shrine, built in [[shinmei-zukuri]] style with plank roofing, faces south and is surrounded by a single {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki}} (sacred fence).<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 245</ref> The shrine measures approximately 1.8 m wide, 1.2 m deep, and 2.4 m high. No {{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/saisenbako|qid=Q135491444}} (offering box) is present.

The shrine grounds cover 228 m² (approximately 69 tsubo).<ref name="sk4">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 244</ref> According to the ''Enryaku Gishikichō,'' the ancient precinct covered about 24,793 m² but has been reduced due to encroachments from private houses, temples, and the Hayasakibunko.<ref name="sk4"/> Parts of the grounds on the north and east sides are lined with {{ill|Stone wall|en|Stone wall|qid=Q979531|lt=stone walls}}.<ref name="sk5"/>

== Ōmizu Shrine ==
Ōmizu Shrine is Ranked 16th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 9–10</ref>

The enshrined deity is Ōyamazumi-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (大山祇御祖命),<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> sometimes written as "大山'''罪乃'''御祖命" in old texts.<ref name="uy0">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 10</ref><ref name="sk3">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 243</ref> This deity is considered a child of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} and {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}}, worshipped as a mountain deity.<ref name="ic"/>

Despite its name, meaning "great water shrine," the enshrined deity is a mountain god, which has puzzled some scholars.<ref name="sk3"/>

== Kawaai Shrine ==
Kawaai Shrine is Ranked 10th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy3">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 13–14</ref>

The enshrined deity is Hosokawa Mizu-no-Kami (細川水神), literally "narrow river water deity," a river god.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>

== Kumabuchi Shrine ==
Kumabuchi Shrine is Ranked 11th among the 16 subordinate shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy3"/>

The enshrined deity is Takiootogi-no-Kami (多支大刀自神),<ref name="ic"/> a guardian deity of sacred springs, considered a child of Ōminakami-no-Mikoto (大水上命).<ref name="gk"/>

== History ==
According to the ''Jingū Auxiliary and Subordinate Shrines Register'' issued in 1880 (Meiji 13), the shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}.<ref name="sk4"/> The ''Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō'' records that a {{ill|Hōri|ja|祝部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shukube|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祝 (神職)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24869239}} was appointed to the shrine, with reconstruction handled by local officials.<ref name="sk3"/> A record from 1482 confirms that the shrine still existed at that time.<ref name="sk3"/>

After falling into disrepair in the medieval period, the shrine was revived in 1664 under the leadership of {{ill|Kawabe no Masanaga|ja|河邊精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe no Masanaga|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="sk2"/> In 1871, Kawaai Shrine and Kumabuchi Shrine were moved to share the same grounds as Ōmizu Shrine.<ref name="sk3"/> These two shrines were originally located upstream along the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}}.<ref name="ic"/>

== Rituals ==
The rituals at Ōmizu Shrine follow the same schedule as those at {{ill|Tsunaga Shrine|ja|津長神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunaga Shrine|qq=}}.<ref name="sk4"/> Ceremonies are held during the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} (February), {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June & December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} (October), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} (November).<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 250</ref> Other rituals, such as the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January 1), {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}} (January 3), National Foundation Day Festival (February 11), {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (February 23), and {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-hi-no-matsuri|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (May & August), are conducted remotely.

== Flora ==
A 1977 survey of the shrine grounds identified 30 trees, including camphor, cedar, fig, chinquapin, and Japanese yew.<ref name="sk5"/>

== Access ==
; To Uji Bridge
* About 15 minutes by {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} bus from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station}} (JR) or {{ill|Ujiyamada Station|ja|Ujiyamada Station|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ujiyamada Station|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Get off at the "Naikū-mae" stop.<ref name="mkr">Mie Prefecture Tourism Federation, "[http://www.kankomie.or.jp/spot/detail_2937.html Ise Grand Shrine (Inner Shrine) Information]" (Accessed October 13, 2013)</ref>
* Accessible from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|en|Isuzugawa Station|qid=Q6089533|lt=Isuzugawa Station}} via Mie Kotsu bus.
* About 5 minutes south via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 32|ja|三重県道32号伊勢磯部線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 32|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357920}} from {{ill|Ise-nishi itnerchange|ja|伊勢西インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-nishi IC|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884865}} or {{ill|Japan National Route 23|en|Japan National Route 23|qid=Q5357579|lt=National Route 23}} from {{ill|Ise interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise IC|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884857}}. Parking is available nearby.<ref name="mkr"/>

; From Uji Bridge
* About 5 minutes (240 m) on foot from Uji Bridge rotary and Naikū-mae parking lot.<ref name="ic1"/>
